To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
when mortality is salient, people are more likely to stereotype.

(a) mortality salience increases negative stereotyping, (b) the effect of mortality salience on stereotyping varies with the nature of the situation, and (c) the effect of situational factors on stereotyping varies as a function of the mortality salience manipulation.
mortality salience increases negative stereotyping in the context of intergroup conflict, but increases both positive and negative stereotypes in the absence of intergroup conflict.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of mortality salience on the formation of stereotypes.
the conditions under which mortality salience increases positive and negative stereotying.
how mortality salience affects the content of stereotypes and how the context in which stereotypes are elicited moderates the effect of mortality salience on stereotype content.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the activation of a comprehension goal leads to a general increase in stereotyping, whereas the activation of an enhanced goal only leads to negative stereotyping.
mortality salience increases stereotyping, but that the direction of this increase depends upon the goals that are activated by mortality salience.
mortality salience increases both positive and negative stereotype content when the situation does not involve intergroup competition or threat.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mortality salience increases the use of stereotyping as a heuristic, and that the content of the stereotypes activated depends on the goals activated.
when people feel that their worldviews are being threatened, they will try to comprehend their environment in order to restore a sense of control.
the activation of a comprehension goal increases stereotyping in general, whereas the activation of an ego-protective goal leads to the activation of negative stereotypes only.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mortality salience may activate a variety of different goals and processes, depending on the situation.
the activation of an enhanced self-concept is not the sole reason for the activation of negative stereotypes.
the effect of mortality salience on stereotyping is not uniform.
